name: pdk-number-parser-etl
instr:
We've started pulling listings from our French-speaking shops, and number_parser can't read them: parse(text, language="fr") just raises. A sample of yesterday's export is in /data/listings/.

French should work the way the other languages already do. parse_number(text, language="fr") should return the integer for any French number from zéro to 999,999,999,999, written the traditional way (deux cent vingt et un) or with the 1990 hyphens (deux-cent-vingt-et-un), and None when the text isn't exactly one number. parse_ordinal(text, language="fr") should read ordinals the same way, with premier and première as 1. parse(text, language="fr") should replace every number and ordinal in running text with its digits and leave every other word as it is; two numbers in a row that can't make one number, like dix-sept dix-huit, come out as 17 18. When no language is given, French text should be picked up as French. Every number in the sample listings has to come out right.

The languages that already work must behave exactly as before, the tests in /app/tests must keep passing, and ruff check and ruff format --check must stay clean with the settings in /app/pyproject.toml. Could you make this work? There's no network here; ruff 0.16.10 is installed.
